# Results — Study 340 (Bank-Loans) on the real total-return tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One question — do floating-rate
**senior bank loans** (BKLN, Invesco Senior Loan ETF) actually protect you when rates rise,
the way the brochure sells them? — run on the **total-return** tapes against **TLT** (20y+
Treasuries), **IEF** (7-10y Treasuries) and **SPY** (equity). As-of **2026-05-31** (last
complete month; the partial June 2026 bar is dropped). Match the fingerprint to confirm you
hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamp

BKLN lists **2011-03-03**, which bounds the joint window honestly — and means the loan
sleeve's first big tests on this tape were the 2018/2022 rate shocks and the 2020 crash.

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| **Joint panel (BKLN, TLT, IEF, SPY, total return)** | 2011-03-03 → 2026-05-29 | 3,833 | `a4d0ad1fb115` |

## The four arms — total return, 2011–2026

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (raw) | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **BKLN (bank loans)** | **3.73%** | **5.8%** | 0.660 | **−24.2%** |
| TLT (20y+ Treasuries) | 2.51% | 14.9% | 0.241 | −48.4% |
| IEF (7-10y Treasuries) | 2.37% | 6.5% | 0.393 | −23.9% |
| SPY (equity) | 14.10% | 17.1% | 0.856 | −33.7% |

BKLN's volatility (5.8%) really *is* low — lower than IEF, a third of TLT — and its CAGR
edges both Treasury arms. The low *rate* sensitivity is genuine. *(Sharpe is raw — there is
no part-cash leg here, so all four arms race on the same footing; label is honest.)*

## Rate sensitivity — does BKLN shrug off rate moves? (the claim)

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| Full-sample beta of BKLN to **TLT** (the rate factor) | **−0.055** (HAC *t* = **−2.95**) |
| Full-sample beta of BKLN to **IEF** | −0.100 (HAC *t* = −2.62) |
| **Downside** beta to TLT (worst 10% of TLT days) | +0.18 |

BKLN's beta to long Treasuries is **essentially zero — and if anything slightly negative**
(HAC *t* = −2.95, robust to autocorrelation). When duration assets sell off on rising
rates, BKLN does *not* follow them down. → the "rate protection" is **statistically real**.

## The rate test — every >5% (rate-driven) TLT drawdown

Did BKLN fall with long bonds when rates rose?

| TLT drawdown | TLT | BKLN | IEF |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2012-07 → 2013-08 | −20.7% | **+5.6%** | −7.7% |
| 2015-01 → 2015-06 | −15.8% | **+1.1%** | −5.1% |
| 2016-07 → 2016-12 | −17.9% | **+3.1%** | −8.2% |
| 2020-08 → 2023-10 (the great repricing) | −48.4% | **+13.9%** | −23.9% |

In the defining episode — the 2020-2023 rate repricing that handed TLT a **−48.4%**
drawdown and IEF **−23.9%** — BKLN **gained +13.9%**. This is exactly what the brochure
promises, and it delivered.

## Where the risk hides — BKLN vs equities (the catch)

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| Full-sample beta of BKLN to **SPY** | **+0.202** (HAC *t* = **+4.48**) |
| **Downside** beta to SPY (worst 10% of SPY days) | **+0.39** |
| beta-to-equity − beta-to-TLT (block-bootstrap) | **+0.257**, 95% CI **[+0.175, +0.349]**, equity-wins **100%** |

BKLN's risk did not vanish — it **moved from duration to credit**. Its beta is to *stocks*,
not bonds, and the block-bootstrap difference (equity-beta minus rate-beta) is large,
positive and excludes zero in every resample.

## The credit test — every >10% equity crash

Did BKLN cushion (like a safe bond), or pile on (like a credit-risk asset)?

| Equity drawdown | SPY | BKLN | TLT |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2011-04 → 2011-10 | −18.6% | −8.4% | +34.6% |
| 2015-07 → 2016-02 | −13.0% | −6.4% | +14.8% |
| 2018-01 → 2018-02 | −10.1% | −0.6% | −3.8% |
| 2018-09 → 2018-12 | −19.3% | −5.3% | +4.5% |
| 2020-02 → 2020-03 (COVID) | −33.7% | **−23.8%** | +14.2% |
| 2022-01 → 2022-10 | −24.5% | −4.8% | −29.3% |
| 2025-02 → 2025-04 | −18.8% | −3.4% | +0.8% |

**BKLN fell in 7 of 7 equity crashes** — and in the COVID liquidity shock it lost **−23.8%**
(its full max drawdown), while Treasuries *rallied* +14%. Floating-rate loans are a
high-yield, illiquid credit instrument: they trade the safety of duration for the danger of
default/liquidity in exactly the moments duration would have helped.

## How to read it

- **The rate protection is real.** BKLN's beta to long Treasuries is ≈0 (HAC *t* = −2.95),
  and it *rose* through the worst Treasury bear market in decades. → Signal **REAL** (on the
  rate-sensitivity claim — the thing the brochure actually promises).
- **It is not a free lunch — the risk moved to credit.** BKLN fell in 7/7 equity crashes,
  carries a +0.39 downside beta to stocks, and lost −24% in the 2020 liquidity event. You
  swapped interest-rate risk for credit/liquidity risk; a modest, real income sleeve, but
  not a safe haven and thin in stress. → Tradability **FRAGILE**.
- **"Rate protection = a free lunch / safe alternative to bonds?" → BUSTED.** Low duration
  is real; *low risk* is not. The 5.8% vol is calm-market vol; in a crisis BKLN behaves like
  the junk-credit instrument it is.
